blacklistabilityReview.evidence: At BSC block 110058930 on 2026-07-15, direct SPUSD token 0x40ff3dea2eec93a7b71879874dc4407918da77a6 was an immutable non-proxy ERC-20 with no global pause or blacklist endpoint. Its verified _update() nevertheless reads the wrapper's getLockInfo(from) and rejects a transfer that would take a time-locked sender below its locked balance before unlock; this is a direct, time-bounded SPUSD transfer restriction. DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE is held by EOA 0xF683ab3aC7dCb195a8dF52D7F5fD796e81A75075 and administers BURNER_ROLE; the wrapper is the current BURNER_ROLE holder. A nonpersistent grantRole(BURNER_ROLE, 0xF683ab3aC7dCb195a8dF52D7F5fD796e81A75075) call from that default admin succeeded. A BURNER_ROLE holder can call the direct token's burnFrom(from, amount), which burns any holder without allowance, so the default admin can authorize arbitrary holder burns. This is a direct Yes. The wrapper's public unwrap only burns the caller's SPUSD; separately, owner/operator controls on the sUSDC conversion route can pause or burn sUSDC and impair conversion, but do not supply the direct-SPUSD transfer conclusion outside the token's own lock check. The documented USDC reserve exposure remains additive. Official docs, terms, and repository were checked; the immutable-wrapper description applies to the wrapper, while this finding is based on verified direct-token source and live role state.
